content.text: The warranty package is complete and favourable to us. No redline is needed — I'll submit a compliant finding.

input.quote: Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
input.rationale: Section 19 delivers the full preferred package in Vendor-binding terms: 19.1 warrants professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a ninety-day Deliverable conformity window running from delivery or acceptance (whichever is later) and hosted-software conformity for the entire subscription term, which under Sections 8.1 and 8.2 (three-year agreement, successive twelve-month renewals) equals or exceeds the preferred twelve-month software period; 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, a no-malicious-code warranty, and no functionality diminution or copyleft contamination; and 19.4 supplies the remedy ladder of re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination of the affected item and a refund of Fees paid. Critically, no disclaimer swallows the express warranty: 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties and expressly states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, and there is no "AS IS" language anywhere in the document. Two minor points short of ideal wording are noted rather than flagged: the no-malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor," and the refund is conditioned on Vendor failing to cure within a reasonable period rather than being available at our election. Neither is a material failure, and the clause benefits us, so we do not redline it.
